## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`requirement_proven` now reports a requirement with no criteria as proven, and this must be fixed before merge because it contradicts the stated "no behavior change" and can let release review pass unverified requirements.

## Changes
The pull request replaces `typing.List`/`Dict` with built-in generics and `log.warn` with `log.warning` in 180 `app/handlers/h*_records.py` files. It also switches `by_name` to `operator.itemgetter`, rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a sum of proven flags with the criteria count, and adds a one-line `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — Return False again when criteria is empty — With `criteria=[]`, `proven == len(criteria)` evaluates `0 == 0` and returns True, whereas the removed `bool(criteria) and all(...)` returned False. The warning on line 10 is logged, and execution then continues to the success result. `tests/test_handlers.py:17-19` has no empty-list case, so the existing test does not catch this. — Release review treats a requirement that has no criteria as proven, so unverified requirements pass. — Fix: Return False right after the warning on line 10, and add a `requirement_proven([])` case to `test_requirement_proof`.
